newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES/ORIOLES RAINOUT MUDDIES PITCHING PICTURE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES/ORIOLES RAINOUT MUDDIES PITCHING PICTURE.

text.p: Tuesday's rainout of the opening game of the American League Championship Series between the Baltimore Orioles and New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium has muddied the pitching picture for both teams.

With Game 1 of the best-of-seven series rescheduled for Wednesday afternoon and Game 2 for Thursday afternoon, a travel day was eliminated and both Yankee manager Joe Torre and Oriole skipper Davey Johnson will likely need a fourth starter at some point in the series.

The two managers had hoped to bring back their Game 1 starters -- Andy Pettitte for New York and Scott Erickson for Baltimore -- on three days' rest in Game 4. But now there will be only two days of rest between Games 1 and 4.
"I'm sure Davey feels the same way I do," Torre said of having to use a fourth starter. "Things happen for a reason and you don't know the results until they're in."
"This is Mother Nature saying she don't want us to play," said Yankee slugger Cecil Fielder.

The series shifts to Baltimore for Game 3 on Friday night and Game 4 Saturday night, as originally scheduled. Game 5, if needed, would be played in Baltimore Sunday with the series returning to New York for the last two games, if necessary, next Tuesday and Wednesday.
Torre had already switched the first two pitchers in his rotation, starting Pettitte in Game 1 with David Cone pitching Game 2 on Thursday.

Cone, who missed four months with an aneurysm in his pitching shoulder, lost the series opener of the Division Series against the Texas Rangers. Since throwing seven no-hit innings against Oakland on September 2, Cone has allowed 20 runs and 30 hits in 31 innings.
Pettitte, the likely A.L. Cy Young Award winner, also was shaky against Texas, walking six in 6 1/3 innings in Game 2.
Kenny Rogers, who did not make it into the third inning of his Game 4 start with Texas, may now get another starting assignment after Jimmy Key works Game 3.

Johnson will switch Mike Mussina, previously set to go in the second game at Yankee Stadium, with David Wells, who had been expected to go on Friday in Baltimore. Wells started twice in the division series against the Cleveland Indians.

"The rainout will affect our pitching," Johnson said. "We'll swap Wells' and Mussina's starts, meaning Wells will go Thursday and Mike on Friday. This will allow Wells to go on full rest and Moose (Mussina) to open at our place. Wells has pitched well here and Moose has done well at our place."
Johnson will be unable to come back with Erickson in Game 4, so rookie Rocky Coppinger or hard-throwing lefty Arthur Rhodes are possible candidates.
The only other rainout in ALCS history was the opening game of the 1971 series between Baltimore and the Oakland A's.

The National League Championship Series has been rained out three times -- twice involving the New York Mets, then managed by Johnson, in 1986 and 1988, and once in 1982 between the St Louis Cardinals and the Atlanta Braves -- who were then managed by Torre.
The Yankees are in the American League Championship Series for the first time since 1981. The Orioles have not been to the ALCS since winning the 1983 World Series.
The winners of the ALCS go to the World Series to face the victors in the NLCS between Atlanta and St Louis which begins Wednesday in Atlanta.
